clue.text: I don't believe it is a request to hear more

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, said to someone spinning a tall tale
taken literally, asking the speaker to go on with a further story

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom of incredulity, and read word for word it also asks for one more story.

clue.text: Drink Scotches neat and sip endless liqueurs

indicators.note: to scotch is to break up or put an end to, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word sip loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone drinks whisky straight while sipping at liqueurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotches' looks like whiskies, but it is the anagram signal. 'endless' cuts SIP to SI; NEAT + SI + LIQUEURS are then rearranged together; 'and' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A tequila sunrise is a cocktail of tequila, orange juice and grenadine, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Inclined to be fast talking

indicators.note: talking means the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A person given to rapid speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast talking' looks like one idea, but 'fast' is the season LENT and 'talking' says it is heard, which gives a word sounding the same, spelt LEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant is the past tense of lean, so it means inclined or tilted.

clue.text: Living accommodation on estate I'm about to develop

indicators.note: the letters are turned about and developed into a new form

explanation.surface: Homes on an estate that the speaker is about to build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to develop' reads as 'soon to build', but it signals that ON ESTATE IM is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a flat on two floors of a building, a kind of home.

clue.text: Missionary in retrospect felt so passionately involved

indicators.note: looking back means reading the letters from right to left
the letters are involved, enclosed, within the run of words felt so passionately

explanation.surface: A churchman who, looking back, felt very strongly about his calling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' finds ELTSOPA inside 'felt so passionately'; 'in retrospect' reads that run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the first Christian missionaries, so an apostle is a missionary.

clue.text: Neat chap supporting cricket side of university

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting word sits below the piece it holds up

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
the on side is a half of a cricket field
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A tidy fellow backs a cricket team from a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is the old word for cattle, not tidy. ON (leg side in cricket) has IAN beneath it in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxonian means belonging to Oxford, so used adjectivally it means of that university.

clue.text: Flog someone for fighting

definitions.meaning: to flog is slang for to sell, and to peddle goods in the street is the same idea
a militant person who favours war rather than diplomacy

explanation.definitionFit: Hawking is peddling wares, and a hawk in politics is a warmonger, opposite of a dove.

clue.text: Tried on, for example, fashionable long coat

indicators.note: the letters are fashioned, made into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone tries on a stylish long coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' looks like praise for the coat, but it signals that TRIEDON plus EG is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A redingote is a long, fitted coat, originally a riding coat.

clue.text: It's the duty of all who succeed to be rich

definitions.text: It's the duty of all who succeed to be rich

parts.words: It's the duty of all who succeed to be rich
parts.note: reads as a moral that the successful must be wealthy; really a levy paid by those who come into an estate of high value

explanation.surface: A maxim that anyone who succeeds ought to be rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty' is a tax, and 'succeed' means to follow someone, as an heir succeeds to an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Heirs pay this levy on a large estate, so it is a duty owed by those who succeed to wealth.

clue.text: Sunday after Easter, when so-called 60s teenager had nothing on

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece put on another follows it

parts.note: quasi means seemingly or so-called
a mod was a stylish 1960s youth on a scooter
O looks like a zero

explanation.surface: On a holiday Sunday a sixties youth went out wearing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had nothing on' suggests nudity, but 'on' just places the zero after the rest. Quasimodo Sunday is named from the Latin opening words of its Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Quasimodo Sunday is the church name for the first Sunday after Easter, also called Low Sunday.

clue.text: Spread fresh lies about woman retiring

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the whole is read from right to left
one piece lies around another, holding it inside

parts.note: fresh means new
Di is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Gossip spreads new lies about a woman who keeps to herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lies about' puts one piece inside the other, making NEDIW; 'retiring' turns all of that round. 'lies' looks like untruths but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen something is to spread it out, making it broader.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about right to be introduced — it's a start

indicators.note: the letter for right is brought into the other word

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
R is the abbreviation for right; that the answer also opens the word introduced is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Someone keen on their rights is being presented, a beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced' sounds like meeting someone; it signals R going inside INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an opening section of a song or speech, so it is the start.

clue.text: Set off for outing

definitions.meaning: to ... an alarm is to set it off

explanation.definitionFit: Trip means to trigger a switch or alarm, and also a jaunt or excursion.

clue.text: Head decapitated long ago

indicators.note: beheaded, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: bonce is British slang for the head

explanation.surface: A head lopped off in ancient times.
explanation.walkthrough: BONCE is British slang for the head; 'decapitated' removes its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, formerly.

clue.text: Heading for disaster with sort of title not for art lovers

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter
a sort of title is a version of it rearranged

parts.note: anti means against, the opposite of for

explanation.surface: Arty types fear disaster from a dubious title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for disaster' looks like doom, but gives D. 'sort of' turns TITLE into ILETT; then ANTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilettanti are amateur admirers of the arts, so they are art lovers.

clue.text: Finish a note not finished the day before

indicators.note: the word is cut off before its end, losing its last letter

parts.note: a chit is a short written note
an eve is the day before a festival

explanation.surface: Completing a note left half-written on the previous day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' trims CHIT to CHI; 'Finish' at the start is the definition, not instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve something is to accomplish or bring it to completion.

clue.text: Narrow-minded, single, upper-class girl taking part in hunt

indicators.note: the girl takes part in, goes inside, the hunt word

parts.note: to hound is to pursue or hunt
I is the Roman numeral one
a deb is a debutante, a young society woman

explanation.surface: A bigoted single debutante joins a fox hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking part in' reads as joining the hunt; it puts the numeral and the debutante inside the verb for chasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidebound means rigidly conventional, unwilling to accept new ideas.

clue.text: Foreign capital one used to back toff holding parade

indicators.note: the piece is placed at the back, after the rest
the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: a nob is a British word for an upper-class person
to air views is to parade them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An overseas capital where someone backs a toff at a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts the parading word inside the toff; 'used to back' puts I at the end. A toff is a British word for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Winning times given in latest reports

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead
dates are points in time

explanation.surface: The fastest race times feature in the newest bulletins.
explanation.definitionFit: Updates are fresh pieces of news, the most recent reports.

clue.text: Is New Orleans a port? Yes

indicators.note: New signals that the following word is made new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A question and answer about whether New Orleans is a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' looks like the city; 'New' is the anagram signal on ORLEANS. 'Is' and 'Yes' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno is a seaport on the west coast of southern Italy.

clue.text: What's said when spotting saint?

definitions.meaning: a person pointing something out says there it is, in the form there is a
St ... of Avila, a Spanish saint

explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is the name of saints such as Theresa of Avila, and sounds like spotting phrase.

clue.text: Long walk one's taken in some built-up London area

indicators.note: the numeral is taken into the reversed word
in a down clue, built up means written from bottom to top

parts.note: part means some
I is the Roman numeral one
SE is the south-east London postal district

explanation.surface: A trek through a heavily built-up district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built-up' turns the word for some upwards, giving TRAP; 'taken in' puts I inside, giving TRAIP, before the postal district.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to trudge, so a traipse is a long, tiring walk.

clue.text: Girl's game that's no good

indicators.note: G stands for good, and the game is left with no G

parts.note: rugby is a ball game

explanation.surface: A girl's sport that is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: G is the abbreviation for good; 'that's no good' removes it from RUGBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is a female first name taken from the red gemstone, so a girl can be called this.

clue.text: Bloodsucker supplying drug chap's about to inject

indicators.note: the drug is put into the reversed name
about means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: Alf is a man's name
E is slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A bloodsucking addict about to inject a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ALF to FLA; 'to inject' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a parasitic insect that feeds on blood.

clue.text: Subject I put in cover note

indicators.note: the letter is put into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: a top is a cover or lid
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone slips a theme into a cover note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places I between TOP and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject of discussion.

clue.text: Given money, about pound, for piece of cloth

indicators.note: the first word goes about, around, the second

parts.note: paid means given money
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone paid about a pound for a scrap of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PAID around L, the pound sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is tartan cloth, or a length of it worn over the shoulder.

clue.text: Fault in puzzle, say

indicators.note: say means this is how the word is heard

parts.note: to floor someone is to baffle or puzzle them

explanation.surface: An error in a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent such as standard British English, FLOOR and FLAW sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaw is a defect or fault.

clue.text: Head has row in discussion

indicators.note: in discussion means spoken, so the word is heard

parts.note: to scull is to row a boat

explanation.surface: A leader in a quarrel during talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like an argument; it is rowing a boat, SCULL, which sounds like the bony head.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull is the bony framework of the head.

clue.text: Sorry about answer given in exercise books twice!

parts.note: re means about, concerning
PE is physical education

indicators.note: the letter is given a place inside the doubled pair
the abbreviation appears two times over

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A pupil apologises for an answer written in exercise books twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'books twice' gives NTNT; 'given in' puts A inside, NTANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being repentant means feeling regret, sorry for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Wall Street figure does own jinxed stocks

indicators.note: a stock is a mixture of ingredients, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Wall Street figure who has his own shares cursed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jinxed' looks like the anagram signal but its J and X are needed; all three words are rearranged and 'stocks' signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dow Jones index is the best-known figure for US share prices.
